clue.text: Foolhardy adjutant's involved in plot

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a plot is a map or chart of an area
ADC, aide-de-camp, is an officer acting as an assistant, like an adjutant

explanation.surface: A reckless army officer gets mixed up in a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme or person is wildly impulsive, which is the same as rash or foolhardy.

clue.text: Account depressing topless Balkan tart

indicators.note: in a down clue, depressing means pressing down on top, so this piece sits above the next
topless means the head is removed, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
a Serb is a Balkan native; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A news account of a scantily clad Balkan woman proves depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' reads as a woman of loose morals; it is the adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare word for sour or sharp-tasting, so it matches tart as an adjective.

clue.text: Plants catnip, oddly, under bottomless container

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the word loses its last letter
in a down clue, under places this piece below the other
oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters only

blocks.note: a can is a container; it loses its final letter
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A gardener puts catnip plants, strangely, beneath a pot with no base.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny desert plants, so they are a kind of plant.

clue.text: Feature of bridge, when holding ace, is to make the first move!

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a pier is a supporting column of a bridge
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: In the card game bridge, leading the ace means opening the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' and 'ace' conjure the card game; the bridge is a structure standing on piers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to be the first to do something, opening the way for others.

clue.text: Rambling among menacing edges on Cheviot

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, at the start and the finish

blocks.note: among means in
dire can mean threatening or menacing
first and last letters of Cheviot

explanation.surface: A walker roams among threatening crags on the edge of the Cheviot Hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cheviots are hills on the English-Scottish border, which makes 'Rambling' look like hillwalking; here it means wandering off the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling speech wanders around its subject instead of going straight to it, so it is indirect.

clue.text: Thoughts of fitting new kitchens and means of paying for them?

definitions.note: a pun: plans for installing, read as INSTALMENT PLANS

blocks.note: first meaning, punning: schemes for installing units
second meaning: hire purchase, paying in regular portions

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a pun: installing a kitchen calls for plans, so they are install-ment plans. The second is the British never-never, buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Instalment plans let buyers pay for goods in regular portions over time rather than all at once.

clue.text: Fill out form for Department and send it

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for department
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bureaucratic instructions: complete the form for the department and post it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fill out' and 'form' suggest paperwork; fill out here means swell.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or expand outward, which is to fill out.

clue.text: Where ups and downs (and location of loos) feature?

definitions.text: Where ups and downs (and location of loos) feature?

blocks.note: surface reading: a map showing hills and valleys
setter's reading: relief also means relieving yourself, so this is a map of places to do so

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a joke on relief in the sense of a lavatory break.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows the height of land by shading or modelling, so its hills and valleys stand out.

clue.text: Hollow performance put up under Cameron's leadership is loudly mocked …

indicators.note: leadership means the letters at the head of the name are taken
in a down clue, under places this piece below the other
in a down clue, put up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the opening two letters of the name
a dell is a small wooded hollow
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A political show staged under David Cameron's leadership is jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow performance' reads as empty posturing; it is two separate words, a valley and an act. The ellipsis leads into the next clue but is only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To catcall is to jeer with shrill whistles or shouts, so catcalled means mocked noisily.

clue.text: Bolshevik put out flag

blocks.note: a Red is a communist, such as a Bolshevik
put out means annoyed, or cross

explanation.surface: A Russian revolutionary displays a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out flag' reads as hoisting a banner; 'put out' is really the adjective meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross emblem, a red cross on white, is a well-known humanitarian flag.

clue.text: Mark's usual loud tie regularly on show

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so only every second letter is displayed

blocks.note: the even letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is wearing his customary garish necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name; it is the definition, in the sense of a gesture marking respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a mark of respect or honour, as in a gun salute marking an occasion.

clue.text: Get rid of biretta Leo's worn

indicators.note: something worn is battered out of its original shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants Pope Leo's tatty clerical cap thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: A biretta is the square cap worn by Catholic clergy, which suits a Pope called Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or destroy completely, a strong way of getting rid of something.

clue.text: Spirit of Dixieland?

indicators.note: of means taken from within, so the letters come out of the following word

blocks.note: sits inside the word, after DIXI

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about the soul of Dixieland jazz, and the answer, verve, really is its spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash, flair or vigour, a lively spirit in performance.

clue.text: I record Mark's riposte about mass in Paris

indicators.note: a riposte is a return thrust in fencing, so the word is sent back the other way
about means surrounding, so this word wraps round the others

blocks.note: taken as written
to log is to record
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes down Mark's sharp reply about a church service in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass in Paris' suggests a church service; it is a unit of mass, defined by a standard kilogram kept near Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilogram is the metric unit of mass, its standard long held at Sèvres outside Paris.

clue.text: … top fiasco developing thereby

indicators.note: something developing changes shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, a huge political flop is unfolding as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for by that very fact, meaning by that means or thereby.

clue.text: Given Falstaff's nightcaps, perhaps, they collapse in the foyer!

definitions.note: a pun: caps worn for a night at Verdi's opera

blocks.note: first meaning, punning: headgear for an evening at Verdi's Falstaff
second meaning: sprung top hats that fold flat in the theatre lobby

explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff is a famous drinker, so the surface pictures drunks keeling over; but Falstaff is also a Verdi opera, and the caps are hats worn at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera hats are collapsible top hats, sprung so they fold flat and can be stored under a theatre seat.

clue.text: Doctor implied I avoided depression

indicators.note: the named letter is avoided, so it is left out
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to drop

explanation.surface: A doctor hinted that the patient escaped clinical depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks medical, but it is a small hollow, as in a cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimple is a small natural hollow in the skin, a slight physical depression.

clue.text: Behind like a bird

blocks.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone is trailing along like a bird following a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for behind or at the back of a ship.

clue.text: Remedy for New Orleans twang?

blocks.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for New Orleans
to twang a guitar is to strum it

explanation.surface: A cure is sought for the drawling twang of New Orleans speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twang' suggests a Southern accent, but it is the sound of plucked guitar strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet scheme, a supposed remedy.

clue.text: Denial by unruly boys swallowing Dad's tablets

indicators.note: something swallowed goes inside the swallower, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: no is a denial
Teds, Teddy boys, were rowdy 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style clothes
Pa is Dad

explanation.surface: Wild lads deny gulping down their father's pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablets' suggests pills, but here they are pads for writing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets in the old sense are flat surfaces for writing, and notepads are paper versions.

clue.text: Scold Just William for being patriotic

blocks.note: first meaning: to reprimand
second meaning: strip the Swiss patriot of his surname and only William is left

explanation.walkthrough: Just William is a series of British children's books about a naughty boy, but here it means William alone: William Tell, the Swiss patriotic hero, with the surname taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone off is the everyday idiom for rebuking or scolding them.

clue.text: Where old king may receive equitable treatment on the way to Oxford, say?

definitions.text: may receive equitable treatment on the way to Oxford

blocks.note: first meaning: an 8th-century king of Mercia

blocks.clueFragment: may receive equitable treatment on the way to Oxford
blocks.note: second meaning: the UK Office for Fair Access, which polices fair university admissions

explanation.walkthrough: Offa ruled Mercia and built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border. The acronym is also the Office for Fair Access, the English regulator for fair admission to universities such as Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The name fits both an Anglo-Saxon monarch and, as an acronym, the body overseeing fair entry to higher education.

clue.text: Pliant chaps, tense in addition

blocks.note: supple means pliant
chaps are men
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Flexible fellows who are also uptight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In addition' looks like a phrase meaning also; 'in' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement is something added to complete or enlarge, an addition.

clue.text: Watered port drunk up by Glow-worm

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards
something drunk is taken inside, so this piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the setter refers to the setter's self, so the pseudonym means me
Rio de Janeiro is a port

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to knocking back a diluted glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Watered port sounds like weak wine; watered is the definition, as in watered silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Moire is fabric, often silk, with a wavy rippled sheen, which is exactly what watered describes.

clue.text: Relative variation in incidence new detectives missed

indicators.note: letters that are missed are skipped, so they are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new; it is removed
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch; removed

explanation.surface: A statistician notes a change in how often new detectives were overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is one kind of relative.

clue.text: Some mercurial celebrity's rejected cake

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used
something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A temperamental star sends back a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry cake filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Mister Satie more imperfectly played

indicators.note: imperfectly means incompletely, so the word loses its final letter
played as in performed freely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man performs more Erik Satie, but badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a form of address; it is the definition, something that makes a mist.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser sprays liquid as a fine spray, so it is literally a device that mists.

clue.text: Gobbles ice creams (about a score)

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is placed round the second

blocks.note: ice creams served in cones
a score is a total, or sum

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down about twenty ice creams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A score' looks like the number twenty; here it is a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to eat it up, and gobbles is a greedy form of that.

clue.text: Supplier receives payment on last of concrete in drive

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the next word is kept
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a fee is a payment
Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
the final letter of concrete

explanation.definitionFit: A feeder supplies something, as a feeder road or stream supplies a larger one.
